Title: Build Reassessment/Threshold Engine
Notes: Per-user counter, threshold-based not real-time/edit-triggered. Raised July 23, 2026. UPDATED Aug 31, 2026 (P11 design session): full tier model locked. Validity floor (not quality) gates whether a reflection counts at all - must contain genuine content (real word), not spam/repeated-character junk; low-quality-but-genuine reflections (even one word) still count. Reflective Density (T-127) never gates eligibility - it only modulates how rich/specific the generated narrative can honestly be. Three tiers: 0-2 qualifying reflections = no narrative, soft directional copy only, no visible count/countdown (avoids gameable target). 3-5 qualifying = first narrative unlocks, thin/honest/affirming even off minimal input (e.g. a single word). 6+ qualifying = same narrative deepens/continues - never restarts as a separate narrative. Regeneration/reassessment is NEVER user-triggered (no manual regenerate action anywhere) - runs automatically, most likely checked on app load, against the local qualifying-reflection count; requires connectivity, and if offline when a threshold would fire it simply runs at next opportunity (no error state, no visible retry). Confirmation loop (T-163): 'Yes, that's me' logs silently in the background, no visible confirmation state; 'Not quite' opens a free-text 'What feels off, or what's missing?' field + Submit, feeding the next reassessment cycle, not an instant rewrite. OFFLINE/ONLINE: narrative text itself is generated online via the shared LLM proxy (T-168) - see T-119 note below for budget - then cached locally as read-only content, viewable offline, never locally re-written by the user. Plain Stats are pure local counts, always offline-available (no network dependency, same as Search/T-128). Rhythm, Intent, 'Yes', and 'Not quite' feedback are real user actions - written locally the instant they happen, synced to Supabase in background, same offline-first pattern as saving a Moment. No Pending/offline UI indicator anywhere on Growth, following the P4 precedent that Save always writes locally first.

Title: Build Prompt Architecture — Classify Today Tab Content by Online/Offline Requirement
Notes: Raised Aug 28, 2026: Kell wants an explicit architecture classifying every Today-tab prompt/card type by whether it requires online LLM access or can run fully offline from local data. Locked classification: ONLINE-REQUIRED = contextual verse (theme-matched via Rich Context/Formation Intelligence, e.g. grief -> grief verse). OFFLINE-CAPABLE (no LLM call) = Question Bank (static rotating list, zero personalization, zero data lookup), Callback card / Continue Your Journey (pulls the user's own capture excerpt into a FIXED sentence template - personalization is which local data is selected, not any generated reasoning), On This Day (pure date-match query against local captures), Random Past Entry (pure random pick, no logic), Photo Callback (pure filter for captures with an attached photo). All four of the latter reuse the same fixed-template pattern as the callback card - none require the system to understand or reason about the content, only to select which local entry to surface. Fallback rule when offline or LLM fails: skip the contextual verse, fall back to Question Bank first (needs nothing but itself). Design pass needed: (1) formalize the fixed question-templates for On This Day / Random Past Entry / Photo Callback (currently only the main callback card's template pattern is designed); (2) write the initial Question Bank list (curated static questions, e.g. 'What's something you're carrying today that you haven't said out loud yet?'); (3) decide rotation/selection logic for Question Bank (random? day-of-week? sequential, no repeats?); (4) explicit note that upgrading any of the offline-capable types to LLM-generated (rather than templated) questions would move them into the online-required column - this is a deliberate choice, not a technical constraint.
